page: Microsoft Azure E32-16as_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the EASv4 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a dedicated AMD EPYC 7763 processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz. The configuration provides 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core. Cache specifications include 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 16.0 GB per core.

For local storage, the instance includes a bundled 524 GB SSD and is capable of utilizing Premium Storage. In benchmark evaluations, the single-core CPU performance via stress-ng is rated as strong, placing in the top 25% with a score of 2707.19. Multi-core CPU performance falls into the average range with a stress-ng score of 21642.12. Memory bandwidth tests demonstrate average performance, with read-only small block cached speeds reaching 1033.94 GB/sec, and uncached large block read and write speeds measured at 51.28 GB/sec and 30.24 GB/sec, respectively.

The server's high memory density makes it qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-intensive workloads that do not require proportional scaling of compute resources. It is well-suited for database operations, as evidenced by its average PassMark database score of 6814.49 and Redis SET throughput of 16.2 million operations per second. Other appropriate workloads include software compilation, web serving, and small-to-medium scale language model inference, where it achieves 34.12 tokens per second for 7B model prompt processing.
